title: Design System: Budget Planner promo page

extensions.scope: Promo page in docs/ only. The Budget Planner app at the project root (index.html, style.css) keeps its own plain look and is not part of this world.

headline.purpose: Page headings on spreads, expanded to width 112%.

title.purpose: The five 'month in it' step headings.

document-caps.purpose: Wordmark and a page's own title, uppercase label green with a hairline rule; cover titles use the same voice in foil at clamp(1.5rem, 3.2vw, 2.6rem).

label.purpose: Uppercase tracked labels for holder fields and residence card rows.

mono.purpose: MRZ line, rates, code chips, the command.

shadows.name: passport-on-cover
shadows.purpose: Filter on every spread; the first layer reads as stacked page edges.

shadows.name: spine
shadows.purpose: Inner edge of each page (mirrored on the left page; moves to the seam when stacked).

shadows.name: laminated-card
shadows.purpose: The residence card on the cover.

shadows.name: stamp-double-rule
shadows.purpose: Not depth: the inner rule of a stamp. Stamps never cast shadows.

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: All transitions and the stamp press.

motion.name: stamp-press
motion.purpose: Stamps press once when live rates arrive; none under prefers-reduced-motion.

breakpoints.name: stack
breakpoints.purpose: Spreads become one column; the opening spread becomes one reordered sheet.

breakpoints.name: phone-narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Stamps drop min-width and the rate line may wrap.

narrative.overview:
The page is one passport, opened on its navy leather cover. Each section is a two-page spread of pale security paper printed with authored green guilloche linework; the visitor turns spreads from the opening page (holder fields, a machine-readable line) through the visa page where three rubber stamps press today's exchange rates in forints, then a month of the real app pasted in like mounted photos, a laminated residence card that states where the data lives, and finally the command to run it. The cover between spreads carries the section titles in foil capitals, as if embossed.

Density is document-like: generous page padding, short measures (46ch), small tracked capitals for field labels, and a single display headline per spread. Ornament is never free: the guilloche, the stamps, the photo corners and the MRZ line are all things real identity documents carry, and each one holds content (a rate, a screenshot, the product name). The page refuses the fintech landing: no headline beside a laptop, no row of three feature cards.
keyCharacteristics: Navy cover as the ground; paper pages as the only reading surface.
Spreads of two pages that stack into one sheet below 860px.
Rubber-stamp inks (violet, red, green) multiplied onto the paper with a rough displaced edge.
Expanded grotesque capitals for document headings; a mono for the MRZ, rates, code and the command.
One laminated residence card on the cover, the only iridescent surface.
Motion is one gesture: stamps press once when live rates arrive.

rules.name: The Two Grounds Rule
rules.body: Text sits on paper or on navy, never on anything else. Paper takes ink; navy takes foil or cover text.

rules.name: The Ink Means Something Rule
rules.body: Stamp inks are reserved for stamps, warnings, and state (violet for interaction, red for over-plan, green for success). No ink as a decorative fill.

rules.name: The Width Axis Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy is carried by Archivo's width axis as much as by size: document voice is expanded (112–125%), reading voice is normal width. Don't introduce a second display family.

rules.name: The Machine Line Rule
rules.body: Mono is for what a machine reads or a person types: MRZ, rates, file names, URLs, commands. Not for labels or headings.

rules.name: The Ink Has No Height Rule
rules.body: Stamps never cast shadows. They are ink multiplied into the paper (`mix-blend-mode: multiply`, opacity 0.92), roughened by the shared `#ink` SVG displacement filter.

dos: **Do** put all reading content on paper pages; the cover carries only foil titles, short notes and the residence card.
**Do** keep stamp inks for stamps, warnings and state: violet for interaction and focus, red for over-plan, green for success.
**Do** carry document voice with Archivo's width axis (112–125%) and tracked uppercase labels in label green with a hairline rule.
**Do** use the mono for machine text: MRZ, rates, file names, URLs, commands.
**Do** keep stamps flat ink: multiply blend, the `#ink` displacement filter, a small tilt, no shadow.
**Do** show the real app in screenshots with demo data, mounted with photo corners.
**Do** stack spreads to one column below 860px, keeping reading order.
**Do** keep motion to the single stamp press, and still for reduced motion.
donts: **Don't** apply this world to the Budget Planner app itself; it keeps its own plain look.
**Don't** build a fintech landing: no headline beside a device mockup, no row of three feature cards.
**Don't** print real-looking ID data (names, birth dates, document numbers) in holder fields or the MRZ; spell only the product.
**Don't** set text on the guilloche green or use foil on paper.
**Don't** add drop shadows to stamps or to text.
**Don't** introduce a second display family or a system display face.
